relevant_to: MySQL/Percona 8.0+ with log_bin=ON and row-based binlog (WRITESET dependency tracking; the only mode in 8.4+). Cannot matter with binlog off, without replicas, or on MariaDB (not present).

signals.metric: binlog last_committed/sequence_number spread (mysqlbinlog on a sample of the run's binlog): mean (sequence_number - last_committed)
signals.condition: the window collapses periodically (last_committed jumps to the latest sequence_number) at a rate matching rows written / history_size
signals.why: when the row-hash map fills it is cleared, so later transactions lose dependency info and replicas can apply fewer of them in parallel

signals.metric: replica: replication_applier_status_by_worker (APPLYING_TRANSACTION timing), replica lag
signals.condition: replica with replica_parallel_workers>1 lags and workers are mostly idle while the coordinator waits
signals.why: narrow dependency windows serialize the replica applier

signals.metric: mysqld CPU profile: share in writeset hashing (Writeset/Commit_order trackers, rpl_write_set_handler)
signals.condition: a measurable CPU share at commit on the primary
signals.why: hashing and map maintenance are paid by every committing transaction

impact_bound: On the primary: at most the CPU share of writeset hashing at commit (normally <1-2%). The real effect is replica apply parallelism, which a single-server benchmark does not measure. Typical: none for primary throughput, low-medium for replica lag.

experiment.change: raise 25000 -> 1000000 (or lower if CPU share is visible)
experiment.predict: mean dependency window in the binlog grows; primary NOPM/CPU per trx unchanged within noise
experiment.confirm_or_refute: window grows with no primary cost -> keep; no window change -> history was not the limit
experiment.cost_or_risk: small extra memory (row hashes) and hashing CPU on the primary

collected: no - needs binlog dependency-window sampling (mysqlbinlog last_committed/sequence_number) and a replica to show the effect

relevant_to: all flavors. MySQL/Percona: crc32 (hardware-accelerated) vs legacy innodb/none; MariaDB: full_crc32 (default) vs crc32, and full_crc32 applies only to newly created files. Cannot matter for throughput when crc32/full_crc32 is already set on a CPU with CRC32 instructions.

signals.metric: perf CPU profile: share in page checksum functions (buf_calc_page_crc32 / ut_crc32* / buf_page_is_corrupted)
signals.condition: a material CPU share in checksum code while a non-crc32 algorithm is set
signals.why: each page read verifies and each page write computes a checksum; crc32 is hardware accelerated, legacy innodb is byte-wise

signals.metric: (Innodb_buffer_pool_reads + Innodb_buffer_pool_pages_flushed) per transaction
signals.condition: with crc32 even high page I/O rates rarely make checksums visible in the profile
signals.why: checksum cost scales with pages read and written, not with logical reads

impact_bound: At most the CPU share of checksum functions in the profile (typically <1% with crc32). Setting 'none' removes corruption detection - never worth it. Typical: none.

experiment.change: only if not crc32/full_crc32: set crc32 (MySQL) / full_crc32 (MariaDB new files)
experiment.predict: checksum share in CPU profile drops; CPU ms per trx drops by about that share
experiment.cost_or_risk: durability: none/strict_* values and mixing algorithms affect corruption detection and downgrade compatibility

collected: yes (CPU profile); checksum symbols may need their own category

relevant_to: MySQL/Percona 8.0.27+ only; matters only during online index builds / table rebuilds (ALTER TABLE, CREATE INDEX). Cannot matter for a DML-only benchmark.

signals.metric: events_stages_*: stage/innodb/alter table (read PK and internal sort), (merge sort), (insert) - time share
signals.condition: DDL is part of the measured workload and merge-sort stage time is a material share
signals.why: the buffer (split across innodb_ddl_threads) bounds the in-memory sort run; smaller buffers mean more merge passes over temp files

signals.metric: file_summary_by_event_name for wait/io/file/innodb/innodb_temp_file during the DDL
signals.condition: large temp-file I/O during the index build
signals.why: external merge sort writes and rereads runs from temp files

impact_bound: At most the merge-sort stage time of DDL in the run; zero if no DDL runs. Typical: none for OLTP benchmarks, low-medium for ALTER-heavy maintenance windows.

experiment.predict: merge sort stage time and temp file I/O drop; total ALTER time drops
experiment.confirm_or_refute: ALTER time unchanged -> scan/insert bound, not sort

collected: no - needs events_stages and temp-file I/O during DDL (only relevant if the workload runs DDL)

relevant_to: MySQL/Percona 8.0.27+; only sort/load phases of online secondary-index builds (not full-text, spatial or virtual-column indexes). Cannot matter without DDL in the workload.

signals.metric: events_stages_*: stage/innodb/alter table (merge sort) and (insert) duration; per-thread CPU during the ALTER
signals.condition: DDL is measured, sort/insert stages dominate and CPUs are idle
signals.why: sort and load run on innodb_ddl_threads threads; extra idle CPUs can be used

signals.metric: CPU utilization and disk util during the ALTER
signals.condition: DDL competes with foreground traffic (foreground latency rises during ALTER)
signals.why: more DDL threads take CPU and I/O from user queries

impact_bound: At most the sort+load stage time times (1 - 1/speedup), bounded by idle CPUs and disk headroom; zero without DDL. Typical: none for OLTP benchmarks.

experiment.change: raise 4 -> number of idle cores (with innodb_ddl_buffer_size raised proportionally)
experiment.predict: ALTER wall time drops; foreground p99 during ALTER may rise
experiment.confirm_or_refute: no ALTER speedup -> scan or I/O bound
experiment.cost_or_risk: CPU/I/O contention with foreground; per-thread buffer shrinks unless the buffer is raised

collected: no - DDL stage timings not collected

relevant_to: all flavors; only pages written by sorted (bulk) index builds - ALTER/OPTIMIZE/CREATE INDEX. Value 100 still leaves 1/16 free in clustered-index leaf pages. Cannot matter if no rebuild precedes the workload.

signals.metric: index_page_splits (and index_page_reorg_attempts) rate right after a rebuild; disabled by default (SET GLOBAL innodb_monitor_enable)
signals.condition: a burst of page splits right after an index rebuild that decays over time
signals.why: fully packed pages split on the first random inserts/updates that grow rows

signals.metric: Innodb_pages_written / rows changed in the first minutes after rebuild vs steady state
signals.condition: writes per change much higher just after rebuild
signals.why: each split dirties and writes extra pages

impact_bound: At most the extra page writes/latching caused by splits in the post-rebuild period; transient. Lower fill factor also costs space and cache hit rate for read-only data. Typical: low.

experiment.change: set 90 (or 80) before the rebuild of tables that are later updated randomly
experiment.predict: index_page_splits and pages written per trx drop in the post-rebuild phase
experiment.confirm_or_refute: no split reduction -> inserts are append-only and 100 is right
experiment.cost_or_risk: larger table, lower buffer pool coverage for read-mostly data

relevant_to: all flavors; changes when a waiting transaction errors out (ER_LOCK_WAIT_TIMEOUT), not how fast work is done. Cannot matter when lock waits are far shorter than the timeout.

signals.metric: Innodb_row_lock_time_max (ms) vs innodb_lock_wait_timeout*1000; Innodb_row_lock_current_waits
signals.condition: waits approach the timeout only during pile-ups
signals.why: the timeout only caps wait duration

signals.metric: events_errors_summary_global_by_error WHERE ERROR_NAME='ER_LOCK_WAIT_TIMEOUT' (MySQL/Percona 8.0+; MariaDB: count errors client-side)
signals.condition: timeouts occur and cause retries that redo work
signals.why: timed-out transactions are rolled back and retried, wasting work while still holding prior locks until rollback

impact_bound: no measurable throughput signal; it trades errors for wait time. Bound = work wasted by timed-out-and-retried transactions. Typical: none.

experiment.change: not a tuning knob; leave as set by the application
experiment.cost_or_risk: semantics: shorter timeouts turn waits into application errors

collected: partly - row lock time collected; error counts by name not collected

relevant_to: all flavors with write workloads; only acts when history list length exceeds the value (0 = never throttles).

signals.metric: trx_rseg_history_len (MySQL/Percona, enabled by default); MariaDB: status Innodb_history_list_length
signals.condition: history list grows steadily through the run instead of plateauing
signals.why: purge cannot keep up; old row versions accumulate

signals.metric: Innodb_buffer_pool_read_requests per row read (or per statement digest) rising as history grows, with unchanged plans
signals.condition: logical reads per row rise with history length
signals.why: consistent reads walk longer undo version chains and secondary-index lookups hit delete-marked records

signals.metric: purge_dml_delay_usec (disabled by default)
signals.condition: non-zero and throughput dropped while history was within acceptable bounds
signals.why: the delay is applied to every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE: (purge_lag/innodb_max_purge_lag - 0.9995)*10000 us

impact_bound: Gain is at most the extra read work attributable to version chains (growth in read_requests per row over the run); it is paid for by writer delay up to innodb_max_purge_lag_delay per DML. Typical: low (stability of long runs, not peak throughput).

experiment.change: set to ~the history length reached in a healthy steady state (e.g. 1M) with innodb_max_purge_lag_delay ~ 300000
experiment.predict: history list plateaus; read_requests per row stay flat over time; write rate drops slightly
experiment.confirm_or_refute: flat reads and unchanged total throughput -> no benefit; throughput lower -> throttling costs more than it saves
experiment.cost_or_risk: throttles DML, can lower peak throughput

collected: yes for history length; partly - enable purge_dml_delay_usec and track read_requests per row over time

relevant_to: all flavors; only when innodb_max_purge_lag > 0 and exceeded. Cannot matter otherwise.

signals.metric: purge_dml_delay_usec (disabled by default)
signals.condition: delay sits at the cap while history keeps growing
signals.why: the cap is binding but not stopping growth: the delay only costs throughput

signals.metric: trx_rseg_history_len / Innodb_history_list_length
signals.condition: history still grows unbounded with the cap applied
signals.why: a higher cap lets the throttle actually slow writers to purge speed

impact_bound: Bounded by purge_dml_delay_usec x DML statements per second as a share of foreground time. Typical: none unless max_purge_lag is used.

experiment.change: set a cap (e.g. 100000-300000 us) together with innodb_max_purge_lag
experiment.predict: history list stabilizes; DML latency rises by at most the observed delay

relevant_to: all flavors (4K-64K); set only at instance initialization - testing needs re-init and data reload.

signals.metric: bytes read per useful row: (Innodb_data_read / Innodb_data_reads) vs average row size of point-lookup tables; Innodb_buffer_pool_reads per row read
signals.condition: I/O-bound point lookups where the hot rows are scattered (one useful row per 16K page)
signals.why: smaller pages cache only the hot rows' neighborhoods, so the same memory holds more hot rows and each miss transfers less

signals.metric: off-CPU share waiting on data page reads of connection threads
signals.condition: a material share AND random point access pattern
signals.why: page size sets read amplification for random lookups

signals.metric: range/scan heavy digests (rows examined per statement high), compression in use
signals.condition: scan-bound or compressed workload
signals.why: larger pages mean fewer page reads and better compression ratio per I/O

impact_bound: At most the data-page-read wait share times the fraction of those misses a denser cache (hot-row density x 16K/new size) would avoid; disk throughput gains if bandwidth-bound. Typical: medium for I/O-bound random point lookups on fast NVMe, none when in-memory.

experiment.change: re-initialize with 8K (or 4K) and reload the same data
experiment.predict: Innodb_buffer_pool_reads per trx and data-page-read wait share drop; disk KiB per trx drops
experiment.confirm_or_refute: no drop -> access is not scattered or data fits in memory
experiment.cost_or_risk: full reinit + reload; larger B-tree height, more page latches/splits, max row size shrinks

collected: partly - row-size / hot-set density per table not collected (information_schema.TABLES AVG_ROW_LENGTH, rows read vs pages read per table from performance_schema/innodb buffer pool stats)

relevant_to: all flavors with UPDATE/DELETE load (inserts create little purge work).

signals.metric: trx_rseg_history_len (MySQL) / Innodb_history_list_length (MariaDB) slope
signals.condition: history grows steadily while purge threads are not CPU-saturated and no long transaction holds an old read view
signals.why: larger batches let purge coordinator/workers process more undo per round

signals.metric: purge_undo_log_pages, purge_invoked rate (disabled by default)
signals.condition: many invocations with small work each while history grows
signals.why: per-batch overhead dominates

signals.metric: CPU / latch share of purge threads and buffer pool reads by purge
signals.condition: purge bursts compete with foreground (latch/off-CPU share rising at purge peaks)
signals.why: large batches touch many pages at once and contend with user threads

impact_bound: Indirect: at most the read amplification caused by accumulated history (see innodb_max_purge_lag) or the foreground time lost to purge bursts. Typical: low.

experiment.change: raise (e.g. 300 -> 1000) when history grows; lower if purge bursts show
experiment.predict: history slope flattens (raise) or latch/off-CPU spikes shrink (lower) without throughput loss
experiment.confirm_or_refute: history keeps growing -> blocked by a read view or purge threads, not batch size
experiment.cost_or_risk: more purge CPU and buffer pool churn

collected: partly - history length collected; purge_* innodb_metrics and per-thread purge CPU not

relevant_to: mariadb only (10.6.18+/10.11.8+/11.4.2+; default ON from 11.6). Changes semantics of REPEATABLE READ; not a performance knob.

signals.metric: rate of ER_CHECKREAD ('Record has changed since last read') errors seen by the client
signals.condition: non-zero after enabling: transactions abort instead of silently updating newer versions
signals.why: with ON, a locking read/write of a row changed after the snapshot fails instead of proceeding

impact_bound: no measurable performance signal; any throughput change is from aborted/retried transactions. Typical: none.

experiment.change: do not change for tuning; keep the application's expectation

collected: no - client error counts by code

relevant_to: all flavors, only for index builds and online ALTER (also sizes increments of the online ALTER row log); MySQL 8.0.27+ parallel index builds are governed by innodb_ddl_buffer_size. Static (restart). Cannot matter without DDL.

signals.metric: events_stages: stage/innodb/alter table (merge sort) time and innodb_temp_file I/O during DDL
signals.condition: DDL is part of the workload and merge sort/temp I/O is a material share
signals.why: a bigger sort buffer means fewer merge passes

impact_bound: At most the merge-sort time of DDL in the run; zero without DDL. Typical: none for OLTP.

experiment.predict: ALTER time and temp file I/O drop
experiment.cost_or_risk: memory per sort during DDL; restart required

relevant_to: all flavors; MySQL needs >=2 undo tablespaces (default), MariaDB needs innodb_undo_tablespaces>=2. Matters only when undo grows beyond innodb_max_undo_log_size (long transactions / heavy updates).

signals.metric: INNODB_TABLESPACES / FILES size of undo tablespaces (MySQL), undo file sizes (MariaDB) over the run
signals.condition: undo files grow beyond innodb_max_undo_log_size and stay large
signals.why: space reclaim only happens when truncation is on

signals.metric: undo_truncate_count, undo_truncate_usec (disabled by default); MariaDB status Innodb_undo_truncations
signals.condition: truncations coincide with throughput dips / stalls
signals.why: truncation marks the tablespace inactive, waits for purge and rebuilds the file; older releases scanned the buffer pool

impact_bound: Disk space mostly; performance cost bounded by throughput lost in windows around undo_truncate events (undo_truncate_usec x frequency). Typical: low.

experiment.change: toggle and run long enough for undo to exceed innodb_max_undo_log_size
experiment.predict: with ON: undo file size bounded; throughput dips only at truncation events
experiment.confirm_or_refute: no dips -> keep ON; dips aligned with truncations -> raise innodb_max_undo_log_size or disable

collected: no - undo tablespace sizes and undo_truncate_* metrics

relevant_to: os (Linux); /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled and defrag. Cannot matter with explicit large pages (large_pages=ON) for the buffer pool.

signals.metric: /proc/vmstat compact_stall, compact_fail rates; PSI /proc/pressure/memory some
signals.condition: compaction stalls occur during the run (THP=always or defrag=always)
signals.why: direct compaction to build huge pages stalls the faulting thread

signals.metric: perf kernel share in compaction / clear_huge_page / khugepaged; mysqld RSS vs configured memory
signals.condition: material kernel CPU in THP paths or RSS bloat beyond buffer pool + buffers
signals.why: huge-page faults zero 2M at a time and allocator holes keep memory resident

signals.metric: perf dTLB-load-misses / page-walk cycles share (perf stat)
signals.condition: high TLB miss cost with a large buffer pool and THP=never
signals.why: huge pages reduce TLB misses on random buffer pool access

signals.metric: /proc/vmstat thp_fault_alloc, thp_fault_fallback, thp_collapse_alloc, thp_split_page
signals.condition: near zero activity -> the setting is not exercised
signals.why: shows whether THP is actually used

impact_bound: Disable: at most the stall time from compaction + kernel CPU in THP paths. Enable/madvise: at most the page-walk cycle share of CPU. Typical: low; high only on memory-fragmented hosts.

experiment.change: switch enabled always <-> madvise/never (and defrag to defer+madvise)
experiment.predict: compact_stall and kernel THP CPU go to ~0 (disable) or dTLB miss cycles drop (enable); CPU ms per trx moves accordingly
experiment.cost_or_risk: RSS changes; benefit of huge pages lost when disabled

collected: partly - add /proc/vmstat thp_* and compact_* deltas and perf dTLB counters

relevant_to: all flavors with performance_schema=ON (pseudo-variable controlling consumers/instruments).

signals.metric: perf CPU profile category performance_schema (pfs_* functions) share of mysqld CPU
signals.condition: a material share (several %) of CPU in PFS code under CPU-bound load
signals.why: each instrumented event costs timer reads and table updates; disabling history/memory instruments removes that work

signals.metric: CPU iowait/idle; run-queue wait
signals.condition: the server is not CPU-bound
signals.why: PFS overhead costs CPU, which matters only when CPU limits throughput

impact_bound: At most the PFS share of the CPU profile under CPU-bound load (minus what lite still keeps). Typical: low-medium (1-10%, higher with history/stage/wait instruments on).

experiment.predict: PFS profile share and CPU ms per trx drop; NOPM rises if CPU-bound
experiment.confirm_or_refute: no change in PFS share -> overhead was in kept instruments
experiment.cost_or_risk: loses statement history and memory accounting

relevant_to: mariadb only (removed in MySQL/Percona 8.0); only when query_cache_type is ON/DEMAND.

signals.metric: Qcache_lowmem_prunes rate; Qcache_free_memory
signals.condition: prunes per second material while hits are high
signals.why: results are evicted for lack of memory and recomputed

signals.metric: Qcache_free_blocks vs Qcache_total_blocks
signals.condition: fragmentation high / memory unused
signals.why: a larger cache costs more invalidation and pruning work under the single cache mutex

impact_bound: At most the time of statements whose cached results were pruned (Qcache_lowmem_prunes x their latency). Typical: low; size beyond tens of MB usually adds lock time.

experiment.predict: Qcache_lowmem_prunes drops, Qcache_hits rises, statement latency drops
experiment.confirm_or_refute: hits flat -> invalidation not memory limits the cache
experiment.cost_or_risk: memory; longer invalidation scans under the global mutex

relevant_to: mariadb only; useful only for read-mostly workloads repeating identical SELECTs on rarely written tables.

signals.metric: Qcache_hits / (Qcache_hits + Com_select) (hits do not increment Com_select)
signals.condition: (when testing ON) a large hit share and SELECT latency share is material
signals.why: cached results skip parse, optimize and execution

signals.metric: Qcache_inserts vs Qcache_hits; Qcache_not_cached
signals.condition: inserts comparable to hits (results invalidated before reuse)
signals.why: every write to a table invalidates its cached results, so caching is pure overhead

signals.metric: perf/latch share in Query_cache lock code; threads in state 'Waiting for query cache lock'
signals.condition: visible latch/off-CPU time on the query cache mutex
signals.why: all lookups, inserts and invalidations serialize on one mutex

signals.metric: digest repetition: share of SELECT executions from a few identical digests with identical literals; table write rate
signals.condition: a few identical SELECTs dominate on tables rarely written
signals.why: only byte-identical queries hit

impact_bound: Enable: at most the share of time spent executing repeated identical SELECTs on unchanged tables. Disable: at most the query-cache latch/CPU share. Typical: none-negative for OLTP with writes; medium-high for read-only repeated queries.

experiment.change: ON with query_cache_size 64M on read-mostly workloads
experiment.predict: Qcache_hits/(hits+Com_select) high, CPU ms per trx and latency drop
experiment.confirm_or_refute: low hit share or rising latch time -> OFF
experiment.cost_or_risk: global mutex contention at high concurrency; stale-read semantics unaffected

collected: partly - status counters yes; query cache lock waits not separated in eBPF/perf categories

relevant_to: MySQL/Percona 8.0+ on Linux (resource groups; not available with the thread pool plugin, not on MariaDB). CPU affinity works without CAP_SYS_NICE; priorities need it.

signals.metric: per-thread run-queue wait (schedstat) of connection threads, correlated in time with page cleaner/purge/log writer CPU bursts
signals.condition: connection threads wait for CPU while background threads burn CPU on the same cores
signals.why: separating background threads stops flush bursts from stealing query CPUs

signals.metric: CPU per InnoDB background thread (performance_schema.threads THREAD_OS_ID -> /proc/<tid>/stat)
signals.condition: background threads use a material, bursty share of CPU
signals.why: sizes how many CPUs the background group needs

signals.metric: Innodb_buffer_pool_wait_free, checkpoint age, Innodb_log_waits after pinning
signals.condition: they rise after confining background threads
signals.why: too few CPUs for background threads slows flushing and redo writing

impact_bound: At most the run-queue wait share of connection threads that coincides with background-thread CPU bursts; costs the CPUs taken away from foreground. Typical: low unless CPU-saturated with heavy flushing.

experiment.change: CREATE RESOURCE GROUP bg TYPE=SYSTEM VCPU=<n CPUs>; SET RESOURCE GROUP bg FOR <page_cleaner/purge/log thread ids>
experiment.predict: connection-thread run-queue wait and p99 latency drop; wait_free/checkpoint age unchanged
experiment.confirm_or_refute: flushing metrics worsen -> background starved; no change in run-queue wait -> not the cause
experiment.cost_or_risk: fewer CPUs for queries; lost after restart unless re-applied

collected: partly - per-thread run-queue wait collected; per-background-thread CPU mapping not

relevant_to: all flavors (MariaDB <11.1 name: tx_isolation). Changes semantics; only try when the application allows READ COMMITTED. With log_bin on, READ COMMITTED needs binlog_format=ROW.

signals.metric: off-CPU share of connection threads in row lock waits; status Innodb_row_lock_time / Innodb_row_lock_waits
signals.condition: a material share of foreground time is row lock waits
signals.why: under REPEATABLE READ locking reads and DML take next-key/gap locks; READ COMMITTED takes record locks only

signals.metric: data_locks LOCK_MODE containing 'GAP' (MySQL 8.0+) sampled during the run; deadlocks: innodb_metrics lock_deadlocks / MariaDB Innodb_deadlocks
signals.condition: gap/next-key locks are a large share of granted/waiting locks or deadlocks occur
signals.why: gap locks block inserts into ranges and create deadlock cycles

signals.metric: trx_rseg_history_len growth with long multi-statement transactions
signals.condition: history grows due to long REPEATABLE READ snapshots
signals.why: READ COMMITTED creates a fresh read view per statement, letting purge advance

impact_bound: At most the row-lock-wait share of foreground time attributable to gap/next-key locks (plus deadlock retries). Typical: none for workloads with few conflicts; medium-high for insert-heavy range-locking workloads.

experiment.predict: row lock wait time and deadlocks drop; NOPM up
experiment.confirm_or_refute: no lock-time change -> conflicts are on the same records
experiment.cost_or_risk: semantics: non-repeatable reads; replication requires ROW binlog

collected: partly - row lock time/waits collected; data_locks gap-lock share and deadlock count not
